card.name: Digits and units in dose tables
card.fires_on: The last digit or unit inside numbers in dose-adjustment tables, such as 0 in 50,000/mcL or 80 mg, or mg and m before /m 2 or /mm 3. It also fires on the start of a word like antimalarial after 'which'.

modes.label: Number endings in tables
modes.description: A final zero or unit inside a lab-count threshold or dose-step number, right before mg or /mcL.
modes.example: Platelet count between 25,000/mcL and 50,00<<0>>/mcL with bleeding Withhold B

modes.label: Units in per-area or count units
modes.description: The m or mg that begins a unit such as /mm 3 or mg/m 2 in dose-reduction tables.
modes.example: 75 mg/m 2 <10 x ULN and 1.26 to 2.0 x ULN 135<< mg>>/m 2 <10 x UL

modes.label: Split word after which
modes.description: The start of the word antimalarial split into pieces after 'which' in a prophylaxis sentence.
modes.example: physicians should carefully evaluate which<< ant>>imalarial to use for therapy.

card.writes: It makes a following lowercase m (as in mg, mm, mcL) more likely and capital M or Me forms less likely.
card.plain: It marks the number or unit spot in dose and blood-count tables where a lowercase m unit comes next.
